messages.author: 789db4736b11c1a8
messages.subject: Adding new aesthetics
parts:
Hello,

how can a new aesthetic be added to ggplot2? Aesthetics defined in aes() are passed to the draw-function of the geoms, without modifying anything.
So this works as I want it to:

df <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10, tooltip = letters[1:10])
ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, tooltip = tooltip), data =df)

But in the next call tooltip will not be passed to the draw function of geom_point.

ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y), data = df, tooltip = "I am a tooltip")

What is the correct way of adding new aesthetics to ggplot2?

If you are interested why I would do something like that: The purpose of this is to write some new geoms, which garnishs the drawn grobs with tooltips for example.
The gTree of the ggplot2 plot will then be converted to a SVG file using the gridSVG package. The variable which was mapped to
tooltip before will now be interactively displayed as a tool tip when moving the mouse over this element.

I hope someone can point me in the right direction!

Best,
Christoph

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Adding new aesthetics
parts:
If you modify default_aes() in GeomPoint, it will do what you're looking for. You could do something like this:
  default_aes <- function(.) aes(shape=16, colour="black", size=2, fill = NA, alpha = 1, tooltip=NA)

I don't know if this is the "right" way - maybe Hadley will weigh in.

You may already be aware of it, but there's also the ggplot2-dev list for questions like this.
-Winston
